title.narrative: # of inclusive policy-making processes (at national level)

description.narrative: # of inclusive policy-making processes (at national level)

comment.narrative: Two policy-making processes initiated in Guatemala have been identified in the baseline. The first one is with the Legislative Commission on Justice Sector Reforms, NIMD is supporting the Legislative Commission for drafting proposals to reform the penal code and the postulation commissions processes to review these proposals technical roundtables are being held with different stakeholders. The second is the support to the Dialogue Group (GAD), they started their discussions in 2019 on political national topics and becoming a dialogue platform, between civil society organizations and political parties to create inclusive policies, laws, amendments, etc. In 2021 they are developing dialogue sessions and NIMD is supporting the systematization of the process.

. It is planned that country offices will aim 2 inclusive policy-making processes during PoD Programme; however, the flexible programming will be adaptative if one country initiates a process and another country cannot fulfill their goal. (Guatemala 2 + El Salvador 2 + Honduras 2)
6 inclusive policy-making processes will be established in Guatemala Regional Programme framework in prior topics based on context analysis as shrinking democratic spaces, barriers to political participation caused by patriarchal, conservative, and exclusionary cultures that place women, youth and other historically excluded groups (such as indigenous peoples) at a disadvantage in decision-making spaces and more. To obtain the planned results by country, NIMD Central America will focus on trust building, commitment among actors and will conduct systematically context analysis to identify political alliances to identify opportunities for inclusive policy-making processes.
